speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the Ministry's assessment on the take-up of the Professional Conversion Programme; (b) what are the challenges in matching and retraining vulnerable professionals amidst increasing retrenchment; (c) what are the take-up rates by workers from different race groups; and (d) whether the Programme has challenges reaching out to specific groups.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Last year alone, we increased the number of PCPs from 22 to 50, covering almost every sector of the economy now.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: However, based on ground observations from our career coaches from e2i and WSG, they have told us that the response across the racial groups is fairly balanced.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In other words, there is a good mix of jobseekers from various racial groups.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: There remains much to do to support the manpower and skills needs of employers and, at the same time, to help our locals who may not have the relevant skills and experience to seize new job opportunities being created.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: MOM and WSG will continue to look at ways to strengthen our support for jobseekers under Adapt and Grow, including through PCPs, in close collaboration with our tripartite partners.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does the Minister have figures  in terms of how many are there who actually applied initially and what proportion was successful that made up this 1,300?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Is there a difference within age groups as well?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, are seniors more difficult to get matched?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: About one-third of those unemployed and managed to find jobs were unemployed for more than six months, meaning they are long-term unemployed.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In terms of breakdown by PMETs and the rank-and-file, again, there is a good balance of about 50:50.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Broadly speaking, our success rate, whether in terms of age breakdown or breakdown by PMETs versus rank-and-file or by long-term unemployed versus unemployed, I would say it has been fairly balanced and fairly inclusive.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But, certainly, I would agree with the Member that for professional conversion, it is more likely that the more mature PMETs may find greater difficulties in going through this professional conversion.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, one observation we made so far is that the majority of the PCPs start at the entry level.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, you move from one profession to another profession, but the majority of them end up starting from the entry level of the new profession.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, this may actually discourage the mature PMETs, because for them to start all over again at the bottom of the new career may be too painful.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is an area that MOM has looked into, whether we should strengthen and enhance the PCPs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: You may hear something on this at the COS this year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In terms of the success rate, again, I have to recall from memory now.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But it does not mean that the other 40% are jobless, because many of them will go through their own efforts, such as applying for jobs through the National Jobs Bank.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In some cases, we have more supply than demand, meaning there were more jobseekers but fewer job openings from employers and, in some cases, the other way around.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What MOM, together with our tripartite partners, is trying to do is to minimise this mismatch.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Again, at the coming COS, we intend to make known further enhancements to the Adapt and Grow initiatives to minimise this mismatch between supply and demand.
